chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who does not know whether he has prayed two rak'ahs or four. He said: He should recite the tashahhud and give salām, then stand and pray two rak'ahs and four sajdahs, reciting in them Fātiḥat al-Kitāb; then he should recite the tashahhud and give salām. So if he had in fact prayed four, then these two would be supererogatory; and if he had prayed two rak'ahs, then these two would complete the four. And if he spoke, then he should perform the two sajdahs of forgetfulness.

key_terms.تَمَامَ الْأَرْبَعَةِ: completion of the four rak'ahs if the prayer was deficient
key_terms.سَجْدَتَيِ السَّهْوِ: the two prostrations performed for forgetfulness or inadvertent error in prayer
key_terms.فَاتِحَةَ الْكِتَابِ: Surat al-Fatihah, recited in the precautionary prayer
key_terms.نَافِلَةً: a supererogatory prayer if the original obligation was already complete
key_terms.يَتَشَهَّدُ: he recites the tashahhud in the prayer
key_terms.يُسَلِّمُ: he gives the salām concluding the prayer

ai.seo_question: What should a person do in salat (prayer) if he doubts whether he prayed two rak'ahs or four?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for one who doubts whether he has prayed two rak'ahs or four. He completes the prayer with salām, then performs two additional rak'ahs as a precaution, which count either as nafilah if the original prayer was complete or as completion if it was deficient. If he speaks in between, he must perform the two sajdahs of forgetfulness.
